claim: For all integers \(b,k\ge 1\), \(\ell\ge 2\), and \(n\ge 3\), let \(Z_b\) denote the b-forcing number: a black vertex with at most \(b\) white neighbors simultaneously turns all of its white neighbors black. Then \[Z_b(P_\ell^k)=\max\{1,\min\{k,\ell-1\}-b+1\},\qquad Z_b(C_n^k)=\max\{1,\min\{2k,n-1\}-b+1\}.\] Equivalently, for every power of a path or cycle, \(Z_b(G^k)=\max\{1,\delta(G^k)-b+1\}\). Thus the general minimum-degree lower bound for b-forcing is sharp on every path power and every cycle power, including the saturated complete-graph regimes.

scientific.integrity: The infinite statement is proved analytically. Exhaustive computation is corroborative only and covers the finite ranges documented in VERIFICATION.md.
scientific.limitations: The theorem is restricted to powers of paths and cycles and does not extend automatically to arbitrary graph powers or other forcing variants.

title: Exact b-forcing numbers for powers of paths and cycles
